title: Kisalian culture of the Upemba Depression
description: People around the lakes of the upper Lualaba bury their dead with fine pottery, ironwork and copper, the forerunners of the Luba kingdom.

title: Diogo Cão at the Yellala Falls
description: The Portuguese navigator sails up the Congo estuary as far as the first rapids, where his men carve an inscription on the rocks.

title: Luba Kingdom founded
description: A kingdom forms in the grasslands west of the upper Lualaba, with a sacred king and a system of government copied by its neighbours.

title: Kuba Kingdom founded
description: Shyaam aMbul aNgoong unites the chiefdoms between the Kasai and Sankuru rivers into a kingdom later known for its sculpture and textiles.

title: Lunda Empire founded
description: A ruler with the title Mwata Yamvo founds a state on the upper Kasai that spreads over much of the southern savanna.

title: Msiri founds the Yeke Kingdom
description: A Nyamwezi trader makes himself ruler of Katanga and controls its copper and the trade routes to both coasts.

title: Nyangwe massacre
description: David Livingstone sees slave traders shoot hundreds of people at a market on the Lualaba, and his report strengthens the campaign against the East African slave trade.

title: Stanley reaches Boma
description: Henry Morton Stanley completes the first recorded descent of the Congo River, showing that it is a route into the heart of the continent.

title: Léopoldville founded
description: Stanley sets up a trading station for Leopold II of Belgium on Malebo Pool, the start of the modern capital.

title: Congo Free State proclaimed
description: With the recognition of the powers at the Berlin Conference, Leopold II of Belgium becomes the personal ruler of the Congo basin.

title: Killing of Msiri
description: Members of the Stairs expedition shoot the king of Katanga and claim his country and its copper for the Congo Free State.

title: Fall of Nyangwe
description: Free State troops under Francis Dhanis take the main town of the Swahili-Arab traders, breaking their hold on the eastern Congo.

title: Matadi to Léopoldville railway opens
description: A line built at the cost of thousands of workers' lives bypasses the rapids and links the navigable upper river to the sea.

title: Casement Report
description: The British consul Roger Casement documents killing and mutilation in the collection of rubber, and an international campaign against Leopold's rule follows.

title: Belgium annexes the Congo
description: The Belgian state takes over the colony from Leopold II after the outcry over the rubber regime.

title: Élisabethville founded
description: The Belgians found a town beside the Étoile copper mine as the railway arrives from the south, and Katanga becomes one of the world's main sources of copper.

title: Simon Kimbangu begins preaching
description: The healing ministry of a Baptist catechist draws large crowds; he dies in prison in 1951, and his church becomes one of the largest founded in Africa.

title: Shinkolobwe uranium sold to the United States
description: Ore from a mine in Katanga supplies most of the uranium used by the Manhattan Project.

title: Léopoldville riots
description: A banned political meeting turns into days of rioting, and Belgium promises independence soon afterwards.

title: Independence
description: The Congo becomes independent with Joseph Kasa-Vubu as president and Patrice Lumumba as prime minister, and the army mutinies within a week.

title: Katanga secedes
description: Moïse Tshombe declares the mining province independent with Belgian support, and United Nations troops end the secession in 1963.

title: Lumumba killed
description: The deposed prime minister is handed over to the Katangan authorities and shot the same night.

title: Operation Dragon Rouge
description: Belgian paratroopers flown in American aircraft free hostages held by Simba rebels at Stanleyville.

title: Mobutu takes power
description: The army commander Joseph-Désiré Mobutu removes the president and begins 32 years of personal rule.

title: Rumble in the Jungle
description: Muhammad Ali beats George Foreman for the world heavyweight title in a fight that Mobutu stages to show off Zaire.

title: Battle of Kolwezi
description: French and Belgian paratroopers drive out rebels from Angola who had seized the mining town.

title: Rwandan refugees reach Goma
description: About a million Rwandan Hutu, among them the organisers of the genocide, cross into Zaire, and the camps become a cause of the wars that follow.

title: Kabila takes Kinshasa
description: Rebels backed by Rwanda and Uganda end the rule of Mobutu, and Laurent-Désiré Kabila renames the country the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

title: Second Congo War begins
description: A rebellion backed by Rwanda and Uganda starts a war that draws in nine African countries and causes millions of deaths, mostly from disease and hunger.

title: Laurent-Désiré Kabila assassinated
description: The president is shot by one of his bodyguards and is succeeded by his son Joseph.

title: Multi-party elections
description: Joseph Kabila wins the first multi-party elections in more than forty years, held under United Nations protection.

title: Tshisekedi sworn in
description: Félix Tshisekedi succeeds Joseph Kabila after a disputed election, the first peaceful handover of power since independence.
